2200 MW. Boundary/qualification: AEMO's 2026 ISP states that after HumeLink is in service the transfer capability between SNSW and CNSW will increase by 2,200 MW in both directions, and the 2024 ISP reports 2,200 MW in both directions as additional network capacity. That is a direction-specific transfer-capability increase on one flow path, not a rating of the line or a single 'network capacity'. The workbook does not define the column. Different dated measures exist for the same project: 2,570 MW of additional firm capacity or generation accommodated (PADR and PACR), 2,230-2,570 MW of Tumut to Sydney transfer uplift (2020 ISP), and REZ hosting figures of +1,000 MW at Wagga Wagga (2020 ISP) and 400 MW in N5 / 2,200 MW in N6+N7 (2026 ISP).

365 km. Boundary/qualification: The NSW planning decision approves development of around 365 kilometres of new double circuit 500 kV transmission lines, and the 2026 ISP records -365 km when HumeLink moved from actionable to committed. Two other archived lengths exist on other bases: approximately 630 km of upgrades (2020 ISP, before the all-double-circuit refinement, where the PADR's three sections were 260 km, 110 km and 260 km) and around 360 km (AER 2022 and AER 2023). The archived 2026 ISP Appendix A5 does not state this itself; its delivery scope enumerates five distinct double-circuit lines (three at 500 kV, one 500 kV built / 330 kV operated, and 330 kV lines between Central B and East), on a different counting boundary from the chart's trunk-line count.
